label: Bible Study
prompt: Let the words of my mouth, and the _____ of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
verse: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
note: The closing prayer of the sky-and-Scripture psalm — many a sermon still begins with it.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Now the God of _____, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
verse: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
note: A benediction for the ages: the God of peace brought again from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep.

label: Sunday School
prompt: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden _____, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
verse: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
note: The KJV's 'cherubims' doubles up the plural — cherub plus Hebrew -im plus English -s — guarding Eden's gate with a flaming sword.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a _____ in the night.
verse: For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
note: Paul borrows Jesus' own image: the day comes unannounced, so live like the porch light's always on.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly _____.
verse: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.
note: Spoken against Eli's house — and slipped to Eric Liddell in a note before his 1924 Olympic 400m final, which he won.
